newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia commodity exports to rise seven pct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia commodity exports to rise seven pct.

text.p: Australian total commodity exports in 1997/98 are forecast to rise to A$62.6 billion, a rise of seven percent on the 1996/97 (July-June) figure of A$58.5 million, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said on Tuesday.
ABARE said in a paper prepared for its annual conference here that by the year 2001/02, the value of commodity exports should have risen to A$69.1 billion.
New capital spending in the mining sector is forecast to rise 25 precent in 1996/97 and investment in metal processing is also expected to increase, ABARE said.
The volume of mine production is projected to rise 21 percent by 2001/02.
Reflecting lower prices for grains wool and beef, the net value of farm production is forecast to be down 29 percent to A$3.1 billion in 1996/97.
A further 17 percent fall is forecast for 1997/98.
Lower prices for most major commodities are expected to result in a fall in average farm cash income in 1996/97, despite generally good seasonal conditions, ABARE said.
In broadacre industries, farm cash income is forecast to fall two percent to average $47,400 in 1996/97.
Economic growth in Australia is assumed to average 3.2 percent in 1996/97 before strengthening to 3.7 percent in 1997/98.
Beyond 1997/98, economic growth is assumed to grow by 3.5 percent, ABARE said.
